GETTING STARTED

Start exploring VOID.

The VOID compiler is in active development. There are no public builds available yet.

Developers with a source checkout can follow the source installation workflow. Start with the prerequisites for Linux x64, Windows x64 or macOS ARM64.

Install from source

VOID needs the complete LLVM/Clang/LLD 23.1.4 development SDK, Python 3.12+, CMake 3.24+ and the platform’s C/C++ development files. A compiler-only LLVM installer is insufficient. Check repository availability before obtaining source; no public binary package or package-manager installation is offered here.

In a source checkout, the source-install helper uses the existing pinned SDK and HTTP dependency recipes, checks downloads and cached inputs, builds the compiler and language server, installs Runtime and standard-library resources, then checks the installed tools. It does not install operating-system prerequisites or edit your shell profile.

Linux x64

The userspace baseline is Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64/glibc. Install build-essential, CMake, Ninja, Python, Make, Perl, CA certificates, xz and the libffi, libedit, LibXml2, zstd, zlib and terminfo development packages. Other distributions need equivalent packages; no lower glibc floor is certified.

python3 tools/install.py --prefix "$HOME/.local"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
voidc --version
python3 tools/verify_install.py "$HOME/.local"

Keep the SDK for later native builds. Add the PATH export to your shell configuration for future sessions. The checkout’s docs/install/linux.md contains exact prerequisites and qualification evidence.

Windows x64

Use Visual Studio Build Tools 2022’s x64 developer environment, C++ desktop tools, Windows/UCRT and DIA SDKs, Python 3.12+, CMake and Ninja. The source helper uses the full pinned LLVM SDK and native Schannel dependency recipe. Follow docs/install/windows.md in the checkout. Earlier isolated developer-host installation passed; the new helper still needs native Windows qualification.

macOS ARM64

Use Apple Silicon, selected Xcode 26+ and its matching SDK/libc++, Python 3.12+, CMake, Make and Perl. Follow docs/install/macos.md in the checkout. Compiler tests cover macOS ARM64, but the new source-install helper has no native macOS installation result yet. A deployment target does not certify execution on that OS version.

Check, run and build

After installing, voidc --help lists commands; voidc run --help explains execution and cache options. Run voidc check main.void, voidc run main.void or voidc build main.void -o hello. Entry selection is automatic. A directory selects exact-case main.void; no entry flag is required.

This is source installation, not independently portable binary packaging. Keep the compiler, matching installed stdlib, Runtime archives and native manifests together. Learn the compiler workflow and configure your editor.
